answer: An agent network can resist Sybils via underwater acoustic ranging. Nodes prove spatial separation by exchanging ultrasonic pulses with receivers fixed to a structural trellis inside a coastal lagoon. Because sound travels slowly through water, an adversary cannot forge arrival delays from a centralized machine and must deploy separate submerged transducer hardware per identity. However, shifting thermoclines alter sound speed, inducing timing errors that falsely reject honest agents.
